literal_meaning: ভাগনে (nephew) কানাই (Kanaai, a name referring to a mischievous or lecherous character)
figurative_meaning_en: A person of lecherous or promiscuous character
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে একটা খাঁটি ভাগনে কানাই, কোনো মেয়ের পেছনে লাগলে ছাড়ে না।
গ্রামের সেই ভাগনে কানাইয়ের মতো সে সবসময় দুষ্টুমি করে।
example_sentences_in_english: He is a real skirt-chaser, just like the nephew Kanaai who never leaves a girl alone.
That guy in the village is as mischievous as Kanaai, always up to no good with women.
history: This idiom likely originates from Bengali folklore tales involving a character named Kanaai, a nephew known for his promiscuous and mischievous behavior, often associated with rural stories around kadamba trees.
note: The idiom draws from traditional Bengali oral literature, emphasizing moral lessons on character flaws.
